items.entity: volume measure V(mu1, mu2, rho) in Eq. (33)
items.description: Eq. (33) requires V(mu1,mu2,rho) <= V0, but V is never defined (Secs. 3.2, 4.1.1). Because X = [mu1*rho, mu2*rho, theta] (Eq. 32), several measures are plausible.
readings: element average of a + b - a*b with a = mu1*rho, b = mu2*rho (solid area of the cross cell)
element average of rho*(mu1 + mu2 - mu1*mu2)
element average of rho only (macroscopic density)

items.description: Sec. 2.1 uses a cross-shaped two-bar cell, homogenized numerically and fitted with a polynomial (Eq. 4). But the Nomenclature calls mu1, mu2 bar widths 'in the Rank-2 microstructure', and Sec. 4.1.4 treats RANK-2 as a separate comparison method.
readings: cross-shaped two-bar unit cell (base E = 1, nu = 0.3), homogenized numerically and fitted by Eq. (4)
analytical Rank-2 laminate stiffness with layer widths mu1*rho, mu2*rho

items.description: Sec. 2.1 does not give the unit-cell mesh, the sampling grid in (mu1, mu2), the polynomial orders q_max and r_max, or the coefficients alpha_ij.
readings: sampling step 0.05 in mu1, mu2 with q_max = r_max = 5
sampling step 0.1 with q_max = r_max = 3
dense lookup table with spline interpolation instead of a polynomial

items.description: Sec. 3.2 gives E = 1 and nu = 0.3 but does not say whether plane stress or plane strain is used, either for the unit-cell homogenization or for the macro analysis.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.entity: bounds rho_min, rho_max and void stiffness
items.description: Eq. (33) uses rho_min <= rho <= rho_max without values, although Sec. 4.1.1 says rho is in [0,1]. As mu*rho goes to 0 the cross-cell stiffness vanishes, so a lower bound or small void stiffness is implied but not stated.
readings: rho_min = 0, rho_max = 1, with void stiffness E_min = 1e-9
rho_min = 1e-3, rho_max = 1
rho_min = 0.01, rho_max = 1

items.description: Eq. (33) requires L_min <= mu1, mu2 <= L_max, but L_max is never given.
readings: L_max = 1.0 (fully solid cells allowed)
L_max = 0.95
L_max = 0.9

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 calls L_min a 'minimum feature size', but Eq. (33) uses it only as a lower bound on the normalized widths mu1, mu2; the effective widths mu*rho can still go to 0. Its length unit is unclear, and so is how to impose it in a single-scale solver.
readings: lower bound on the normalized mu1, mu2 only, exactly as in Eq. (33)
lower bound on the effective widths mu1*rho, mu2*rho wherever rho > 0
physical minimum member size of L_min x macro-element size (or x domain height), imposed through a length-scale filter or projection

items.description: Eq. (31) brings rho in only through C^H(mu1*rho, mu2*rho). Sec. 4.1.1 says rho should separate void regions from lattice-filled ones, but no penalty exponent or projection that pushes rho to 0/1 is described.
readings: no extra penalization (rho enters only as in Eq. 31)
SIMP-type power, e.g. C^H(mu1*rho^3, mu2*rho^3) or rho^3*C^H
Heaviside projection of filtered rho, with beta increased step by step
